wu: Headline Race: Students form teams. Each team gets 5 news headline flashcards. They race to match them to the correct news category (politics, sports, entertainment, technology, local) on the board. The first team to match all correctly wins points.
wuAlt: News Source Sort: Students sort a pile of news source cards (TV, radio, newspaper, blog, social media) into 'trustworthy' and 'less trustworthy' piles and explain why.
Opinion Line: Students stand in a line. The teacher reads a news topic (e.g., 'Social media is good for news'). Students move to the left (agree) or right (disagree) and say one reason.
pres: Show a short video clip of a news bulletin. Introduce media vocabulary (e.g., 'headline', 'source', 'bias', 'fact', 'opinion') using flashcards with images. Model sentences: 'I think... because...' and 'For example...'. Check understanding by asking students to categorize words as fact or opinion.
presAlt: Realia Display: Bring in a newspaper, a phone showing a news app, and a radio. Elicit the names and ask students to compare them. Use a Venn diagram on the board to show similarities and differences.
Role Model: Teacher plays a news anchor, then a biased commentator. Students identify the difference in language and label the examples on the board.
prac: Headline Matching: Students work in pairs. They receive a worksheet with 5 headlines and 5 short news summaries. They match them, then practice saying: 'This headline is about... because...'. Teacher monitors and corrects pronunciation.
pracAlt: Opinion Frames Drill: In groups, students get a list of news topics. They take turns completing the frame: 'In my opinion, [topic] is [adjective]. For example, [example]. This is because [reason]'.
Media Bingo: Each student gets a bingo card with media vocabulary (e.g., 'breaking news', 'editorial'). The teacher reads definitions, and students mark the words.
ls: Listening to a news podcast: Students listen to a 2-minute bulletin about a local Moroccan issue (e.g., tourism). They complete a table with 'Who', 'What', 'Where', 'Why'. They then compare in pairs before class feedback.
re: Quick Debate: Students stand. The teacher says a news topic (e.g., 'AI in news'). Students quickly turn to a partner and state their opinion with one reason using 'I believe... because...'. After 30 seconds, switch partners.
prod: News Panel Discussion: Students form groups of 4. Each group is a panel discussing 'Are social media news sources reliable?'. They assign roles (moderator, two panelists, audience). They prepare for 5 mins, then discuss for 8 mins using frames: 'I agree with [name] because...' and 'On the other hand...'.
rw: Reading and Writing: Students read a short, simplified news article about a Moroccan festival (e.g., Rose Festival). They underline 3 facts. Then, they write a 80-word opinion paragraph using the frame: 'I think this festival is important because... For example...'.
st: Story + Goodbye: Read a short news story about a positive event in Morocco (e.g., a community project). End with: 'Today, you practiced giving opinions about news. Thank you for your thoughtful contributions. Have a great day!'
g: Teams match headlines to categories on the board.
Students move left/right for agree/disagree and state a reason.
Students mark vocabulary words as the teacher defines them.
Partners state opinions on news topics with reasons.
Groups discuss reliability of social media news in assigned roles.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a second opinion paragraph arguing the opposite view of their first one.
Support / weaker learners: Use a sentence frame worksheet to write their opinion paragraph.
hw: Watch a 5-minute news segment. Write 3 facts and 1 opinion in your notebook.
Choose a news topic from class. Write a 100-word paragraph using 'I think... because... For example...'.
Interview a family member about their favorite news source. Write 3 sentences about their choice.
tip: Encourage students to connect news topics to their lives in Morocco, e.g., discussing how global news affects local issues. This builds relevance and confidence.
